findings.problem: This is a 17-line proof that an odd-cardinality finite field has odd prime-power order. It writes the order as p^n via `FiniteField.card'`, then shows p = 2 forces an even order. The proof is copied verbatim into `isOddPrimePower_of_L2Field` in L2/Transport.lean (lines 81-95). The only difference is the final hypothesis, `h.1` instead of `h`, and `h.1` is exactly `Odd (Nat.card F)`. The same fact is also proved in other files, with shorter proofs. `ABGLocalTools.isOddPrimePower_card_of_odd` uses `card_eq_ringChar_pow` and `ringChar_prime.odd_of_ne_two` in 4 lines, and there are private copies in PSL2FourGroups.lean and Odd87L2Card.lean. So the by_contra / p = 2 / `Nat.even_pow` argument is maintained in several places.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one canonical lemma `isOddPrimePower_of_odd_card {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (h : Odd (Nat.card F)) : IsOddPrimePower (Nat.card F)`. Put it in a file that both users import, such as IVK.Defs or a small new lower-level file; if Transport can import FixedPGL, it can stay here. Give it a short proof along the lines of the existing shorter version: obtain `⟨f, hf, hq⟩ := card_eq_ringChar_pow (F := F)`, then `refine ⟨ringChar F, f, ringChar_prime, ?_, hf, hq⟩` and conclude with `ringChar_prime.odd_of_ne_two (ringChar_ne_two_of_odd_card h)`. Alternatively use the `Nat.odd_pow_iff` route from PSL2FourGroups.lean. Then replace the body of `isOddPrimePower_of_L2Field` in Transport.lean with `isOddPrimePower_of_odd_card h.1`, or delete it and use `isOddPrimePower_of_odd_card hF.1` at its call sites. The call sites are Lemma19c.lean:128, KI2Aux.lean:44, Transport.lean:102 and :150, Sec3Fac.lean:758, and Lemma14h.lean:181. The same lemma should replace the private copy in Odd87L2Card.lean and, where the import graph allows, the other private copies. Both uses then are one-line wrappers under their real hypotheses: `h : Odd (Nat.card F)` in the target and `h : L2Field F` (whose first component is `Odd (Nat.card F)`) in Transport.
findings.benefit: The odd-order-to-odd-prime-power argument has a single maintained proof instead of two identical 15-line blocks plus further private variants. A reader of either file sees a one-line reduction to a named fact. Fixes or proof-engineering updates (for example to `FiniteField.card'`) then happen in one place.
